cases.text: the patient is Thrandia and she is stable

expect.filtered_text: the patient is {{{REDACTED-first-name}}} and she is stable

rationale: A first name mid-sentence. The names come from the policy, so the case asserts detection rather than the contents of a word list shipped inside an implementation.

cases.text: Thrandia and Melisor both signed in
rationale: Two names in one document must produce two spans, in order of appearance.

cases.text: the patient is thrandia in lowercase
rationale: A name is the same name however it is cased, so matching ignores case. Easy to get wrong when porting, because the underlying lookup is usually a set.

cases.text: the patient is Aaban and he is stable

expect.filtered_text: the patient is Aaban and he is stable

rationale: 'Aaban' is in the first name list Phileas bundles, in both the production copy and the fixture that shadows it on the test classpath. The policy does not supply it.

Terms given in the policy replace the bundled list rather than adding to it, so a name the policy does not list is not found. This is what makes the case portable: an implementation shipping a different word list gives the same answer.
A document holding no name from the policy produces no spans.
